argument_summary: The strongest admissible defense is narrower than the original claim. The record supports that the release is launch-ready in aggregate because it clears aggregate readiness by 2.1 percentage points and had no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and public governance sources support certification decisions that document limitations and continue measurement rather than requiring zero residual risk. But the same admissible record also shows the small-business onboarding gap is tied to a named customer segment and an open legal question, so aggregate readiness does not by itself resolve the disclosure issue. The audit concern should therefore be narrowed from broad noncompliance on certification to a caveated conclusion: certification is supportable on aggregate readiness grounds, while support is weak on certification without disclosure or approved risk acceptance.
claims_about_business_cost: The business-cost point is limited: escalation would delay the planned Friday launch path, but the admissible record does not support using cost as a substitute for the policy predicates. At most, cost supports handling the remaining issue through a bounded caveat and targeted follow-up rather than treating aggregate readiness as valueless.
claims_about_policy: The governing policy separates launch readiness from treatment of material limitations. Aggregate readiness evidence is relevant to whether the model is fit for release in general, but the policy text indicates a weakness is material when it affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case, and product labels like non-core do not defeat materiality when customer commitments or pending legal review exist. On the admissible record, the small-business onboarding issue is material enough to trigger the disclosure-or-accepted-risk requirement unless resolved. That means the best policy-grounded position is not that disclosure is unnecessary, but that the certification record can be treated as caveated rather than wholly unsupported.
concessions: There is no admissible evidence of finalized legal clearance on whether the gap must be disclosed.
There is no admissible evidence of approved risk acceptance for launch with this unresolved limitation.
There is no admissible evidence that the limitation has already been disclosed in launch materials or a model card.
The small-business onboarding segment is harder to treat as immaterial because it is named in two paid pilot commitments.
The policy record limits any defense of certification without disclosure to a weak, caveated form.
